messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] besagproper 2 vs BYM2
parts:
its always hard to compare directly these marked numbers as the
besagproper model is not scaled hence the values are not directly
comparable, but I guess you're refering to one `high' and one 'low'
'Lambda', which is not in coherence with what you get with the bym2.

the bym2 is constructed to be more stable and give interpretable
results, and I do not have enough experience with the 'besagproper2'
one. 

I am not even convinced that the '...proper2' and '...proper' ones are
the correct way of making them proper, but I guess that is another
issue.

I do find that the Leroux construction does not make much sense to me,
as its a convex combination of precision matrices, which has not
interpretation in this context. the interpretation of the paramters does
not make sense (hence priors becomes 'hard'), and the bym2 model is the
``correct'' answer to what they had in mind. so to me, the Leroux (and
those built on that), is more a method than a model. I discuss this
issue in this talk

http://www.birs.ca/events/2017/5-day-workshops/17w5153/videos/watch/201712040907-Rue.html

but that is just my view.


I guess there are things to do to verify the results.

r = inla(....)

then rerun to verify stability

r = inla.rerun(r)


also check with the new mode,

library(INLA)
inla.setOption(inla.mode="experimental")

r = inla(...)


that the results are stable


if you're in doubt, I can rerun them here if you like

Best
H
